subject: Physics
subtopic: Newton's first law and free-body diagrams
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic while practice support is routed separately.

rungs.aha: Zero net force does not mean zero motion: it means the velocity does not change, so rest and constant-velocity motion are both possible.
learner_owns: Can describe whether an object's speed or direction is changing.
must_contain: A case that keeps moving after the push has ended.
A case at rest with no change in motion, treated by the same rule.

misconception.wrong_idea: A force must keep acting in the direction of motion or the object must stop.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A low-friction cart is pushed and then released. After the hand loses contact, what horizontal force is required merely to keep it moving steadily?
misconception.repair: Separate velocity from change of velocity: a net force is required for acceleration, not for the existence of motion.

rungs.closure: Given a motion description, state whether zero net force is compatible with it and justify the decision from whether velocity changes.

controlled_variation.vary: whether a brief push is still in contact
controlled_variation.hold: the cart's direction and an approximately frictionless surface after release
controlled_variation.notice: the cart can continue moving after the applied push becomes zero

controlled_variation.vary: the initial velocity from zero to nonzero
controlled_variation.notice: both rest and steady motion fit the same zero-change condition

rungs.aha: Several forces can act on one body while their vector sum is zero; the motion responds to the sum, not to the mere presence of forces.
learner_owns: Zero net force does not mean zero motion: it means the velocity does not change, so rest and constant-velocity motion are both possible.
must_contain: At least two nonzero force arrows whose vector sum is zero.
A comparison between 'no force' and 'zero net force'.

misconception.wrong_idea: If the net force is zero, no forces are acting.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A book rests on a table. Are there no forces on the book, or can nonzero forces add to zero?
misconception.repair: List every interaction force on the body, then add them as directed quantities; cancellation belongs to the sum, not to the individual forces.

rungs.closure: For a stationary or steadily moving object, identify a nonzero force pair that can sum to zero and show their directions.

controlled_variation.vary: the magnitudes of two opposite collinear forces together
controlled_variation.notice: the individual arrows can grow while the net arrow remains zero

rungs.aha: A free-body diagram contains forces acting on the chosen body only; an action-reaction partner acts on the other body and belongs on its diagram.
learner_owns: Several forces can act on one body while their vector sum is zero; the motion responds to the sum, not to the mere presence of forces.
must_contain: The same interaction shown on two separate body diagrams.
A rule that every arrow on one diagram must name an external agent acting on that chosen body.

misconception.wrong_idea: Equal and opposite interaction forces cancel each other on one body's free-body diagram.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A horse pulls a cart and the cart pulls back equally. Which of those two forces acts on the cart, and which acts on the horse?
misconception.repair: Choose one body first. Put only forces acting on that body on its diagram; draw the partner force only when the other body is chosen.

rungs.closure: Given two interacting bodies, draw or describe separate force inventories and place an action-reaction pair on different bodies.

controlled_variation.notice: the equal-and-opposite partner arrow moves to the other body's diagram rather than cancelling on one diagram

controlled_variation.vary: an additional external horizontal force on one body
controlled_variation.hold: the interaction pair between the two bodies
controlled_variation.notice: the two bodies can have different net forces even though the interaction pair remains equal and opposite

rungs.aha: Newton's force law needs a declared frame: in an accelerating frame an added pseudo-force is required to recover the same observed acceleration.
learner_owns: A free-body diagram contains forces acting on the chosen body only; an action-reaction partner acts on the other body and belongs on its diagram.
must_contain: Two observers describing the same object, one in a non-accelerating frame and one in an accelerating frame.
An explicit declaration of the chosen frame before the force sum is written.

misconception.wrong_idea: The same ordinary-force diagram can be used unchanged in any accelerating observer's frame.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A mass appears to accelerate backward inside a bus that starts forward. Can the bus-frame observer use only the same real-force inventory as the roadside observer?
misconception.repair: Either analyse in an inertial frame using real interactions, or if using an accelerating frame include the frame's pseudo-force consistently.

rungs.closure: Given a simple accelerating-frame situation, state which frame is being used and whether a pseudo-force must be included.

controlled_variation.vary: the observer from roadside to steadily moving bus
controlled_variation.hold: the physical interactions and the bus's zero acceleration
controlled_variation.notice: no extra force is needed when the frames differ only by constant velocity

controlled_variation.vary: the bus from steady speed to forward acceleration
controlled_variation.hold: the same object and physical interactions
controlled_variation.notice: the bus-frame account now needs an added backward pseudo-force

family.invariant_demand: Choose the body and frame, identify only forces acting on that body, add them as directed quantities, and use the net force to decide or determine the body's acceleration.
family.difficult_move: Choosing the body boundary correctly so interaction partners are not accidentally cancelled on the same free-body diagram.
family.independent_check: Every force arrow must name an external agent acting on the chosen body, and the direction of the vector sum must agree with the stated acceleration.

support_ladder.handed_over: The target body, coordinate directions, and a list of candidate interactions are supplied.
The target body and coordinate directions are supplied.
Only the physical situation and requested acceleration or force are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: The problem is described from inside an accelerating vehicle and the learner must choose an inertial-frame analysis or add a pseudo-force.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the chosen observer frame is inertial

transfer.changed_demand: A contact-and-motion sketch must be converted into separate free-body diagrams before any equations are written.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which interactions act on each chosen body

transfer.changed_demand: Two connected bodies must be analysed with one free-body diagram per body and the shared interaction linked across the equations.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which equal-and-opposite forces belong to different equations
